solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Nuptial bed is pounded, it's certain

indicators.note: something pounded is battered out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that wedding-night bedding has been well tested, and that's a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounded' rearranges NUPTIALBEDIS, all twelve letters of the first three words; 'it's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond dispute is sure and settled, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Criminal, wicked convict brought up possessing Ecstasy

indicators.note: possessing means the pieces hold another letter inside them

parts.note: ill can mean evil or wicked, as in ill deeds

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lag is slang for a convict, especially an old lag
E is the standard abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A wicked convict is hauled up for holding ecstasy, a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun for the convict, but it is the adjective defining the answer; a lag is British slang for a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something against the law, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Discourage the German and French in embrace

indicators.note: in embrace means the first piece wraps its arms round the second

parts.note: der is a German word for the
et is French for and

explanation.surface: An attempt to put off a German and a Frenchman who are hugging.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone from acting is to put them off, a synonym.

clue.text: Tie given by tasteless wife

parts.note: stale food has lost its taste
a mate is a spouse or partner

explanation.surface: A drawn result produced by a dull wife.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess a STALEMATE is a drawn game, so it is a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock or draw in which neither side can win, as in chess.

clue.text: Removal, taking top off, provokes desire

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: a purge is a removal of unwanted people or things

explanation.surface: Getting rid of something by beheading stirs up longing.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a strong desire or impulse, a synonym.

clue.text: Trace son in order to reveal forefather

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: Tracking down a son to discover a forebear, as in genealogy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges TRACESON; 'to reveal' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is someone you are descended from, the same as a forefather.

clue.text: Restricted Liberal leader over state

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
Cal is an abbreviation of California, a US state

explanation.surface: A Liberal party leader is said to be above the condition of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Local means confined to a particular area, so limited or restricted in scope.

clue.text: Country's Government leader trapping Opposition leader

indicators.note: trapping means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: David Cameron was the UK Prime Minister when this puzzle appeared

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A nation's prime minister holds the leader of the opposition in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Country's' stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. Cameron was British PM 2010-16.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameroon is a country in west-central Africa.

clue.text: One's repeatedly under credit crunch

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below the other piece

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: repeatedly means this piece is given twice

parts.note: one is I, and 's adds S

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going under during the credit crunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'credit crunch' as one phrase, but 'credit' gives CR and 'crunch' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crunch is a critical moment or emergency, the same as a crisis.

clue.text: Heavy charge lit to explode

indicators.note: something that explodes is blown apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A heavy explosive charge is lit and goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy here means sluggish and drowsy, as in heavy eyelids, a synonym.

clue.text: Tea around one for lounger, perhaps

indicators.note: around means the tea word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: char is informal British for tea
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Tea is brought round for someone lazing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shows the definition is by example: a lounger is one kind of seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounger is a kind of reclining seat, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: Grand talent by Queen's supporting band?

parts.note: G is a common abbreviation for grand, a thousand
art is skill or talent
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A gifted musician alongside Queen as a backing group.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on Queen the rock band; the definition reads 'band' as an elastic strip holding up a stocking.
explanation.definitionFit: A garter is an elastic band worn to hold up a stocking or sock.

clue.text: Small changes on page for religious texts

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
alters means changes

explanation.surface: Minor edits to a page of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalters are books containing the Psalms, used in worship.

clue.text: In bathroom, female with a hard sponge

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet or bathroom
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A woman in the bathroom with a rough scrubber.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is a fibrous plant pod dried and used as a bath sponge.

clue.text: Speeches over budgets

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
rations are fixed allowances, budgeted amounts

explanation.surface: Ministers make speeches about budgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Orations are formal public speeches, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Opulent old American after feed

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the feed word

parts.note: to gorge is to feed greedily
US stands for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: A rich old American following a big meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgeous can mean richly splendid or sumptuous, close to opulent.

clue.text: End of testing finished head teacher

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: over means finished
a ness is a headland, a head projecting into the sea

explanation.surface: Testing is over for the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head teacher' looks like one title, but 'head' is wordplay and 'teacher' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A governess is a woman employed to teach children in a private household.

clue.text: Metamorphosis of larvae in plant

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a complete change of form, so the letters are transformed

explanation.surface: Caterpillars changing into adults on a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metamorphosis of' rearranges LARVAEIN, which includes the little word 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Valerian is a flowering plant whose root is used as a herbal sedative.

clue.text: Possibly Armstrong's small step with crew

definitions.note: Neil Armstrong is an example, so possibly; the 's means is

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a pace is a single step
to man a vessel is to crew it

explanation.surface: Neil Armstrong's famous small step taken with his crew.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls 'one small step for man', but each word is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong, first man on the Moon, is an example of an astronaut.

clue.text: Sculpting bust, the French getting artful

indicators.note: sculpting shapes material anew, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French sculptor carving a bust with skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sculpting' rearranges BUST to SUBT; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtle can mean clever and crafty, the same as artful.

clue.text: First woman's hugging including display

indicators.note: hugging means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis; the 's is a link
inc is an abbreviation for including

explanation.surface: Eve embraces everyone in a show of affection.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to show or display it.

clue.text: Document, it legally covers permit

indicators.note: covers means the clue words conceal the answer among them

explanation.surface: A legal document granting authorisation.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them the right, that is to permit or authorise.

clue.text: Turn gay in seaside town, say

indicators.note: say means the word is to be spoken out loud

parts.note: Brighton is a resort on the English south coast

explanation.surface: Coming out in a famously gay-friendly English seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Gay is used in its older sense of cheerful; Brighton is a south-coast resort famous for its gay scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To brighten is to become cheerful, and gay once meant merry.

clue.text: Person of faith in Durgapur?

indicators.note: of here means made from part of, so the letters are drawn from inside the following words

explanation.surface: Asking what religion someone in an Indian city follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the last letter of 'faith' and ends in 'Durgapur'. Durgapur, a city in West Bengal named after the goddess Durga, makes the whole clue a fair description too.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the main religion of India is a person defined by that faith.

clue.text: Mine includes endless wine, cheers!

indicators.note: includes means the mine word holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine

explanation.surface: A miner drinks a toast with some wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German drinking toast, like cheers.

clue.text: Revolution engulfing a country

indicators.note: engulfing means the first piece swallows up the second

parts.note: a spin is a turn or revolution

explanation.surface: An uprising sweeps over a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests a political uprising, but it is a turning motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a country in south-western Europe.

clue.text: Start to eat after little nibble

indicators.note: after means the first letter goes behind the other piece

parts.note: a bit is a little amount

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Begin eating after a small snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A bite is a small mouthful, the same as a nibble.

clue.text: Revolutionary Labour leader with odd number returned

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
returned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: nine is an odd number

explanation.surface: A radical Labour leader comes back with a strange figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Russian Revolution of 1917, a famous revolutionary.

clue.text: One can cry about sweetheart's wandering

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go round the next one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a tin is a can
to rant is to shout or cry out angrily
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: Someone who can cry over a lover's roving eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is the classic crossword E, the centre letter of 'sweet'; 'wandering' looks like an anagram signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant person travels from place to place, so wandering.

clue.text: Buzzing insects and queen producing purest substance

indicators.note: buzzing suggests frantic activity, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A hive of buzzing bees and their queen produces pure honey.
explanation.definitionFit: The quintessence is the purest, most concentrated essence of something.
